title: An inference stack that survives
intro: Design the production serving topology — then read the physics tiles under the board.
briefing: Wire a production LLM serving stack: users reach vLLM replicas only through a gateway, replicas pull weights from a model registry, and **no single node failure may cut users off from the models**. The live tiles under the board score your topology as you build.

rules.label: No client talks straight to a replica
Replicas pull weights from the registry
No single point of failure users → models

debrief: The shape that passes: two gateways, two-plus replicas, a reachable registry, cross-wired so every middle node is bypassable. The part most designs miss is the front door — one gateway is a single point of failure no matter how many replicas sit behind it. Continuous batching makes each replica efficient; the topology makes the fleet survive.
